name: Dalton Omondi Opondo
engineeringObjective: Electrical & Electronics Engineering student at Kenyatta University building AI assessment infrastructure, embedded hardware systems, and scalable education technologies across Africa.
researchStatement: AI engineer & Olympiad trainer investigating neural architecture co-design, reasoning benchmarks (ARC Prize, AIMO), structured sparsity (ZPSN), and silicon photonics for next-generation intelligent systems.
bio: Building intelligent systems at the intersection of AI, embedded engineering, and education. Founder of Proctor AI, IEEEXtreme 18.0 Rank #1 team in Kenya, IEEE Tech Ignite 1st Runner-Up, International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) participant, and Chief Trainer for the Kenya Mathematical Olympiad.

about.approach: My work is driven by a simple philosophy: building systems over performing personal branding. Whether I am architecting Proctor AI to assess tens of thousands of Olympiad candidates across East Africa, competing in high-stakes programming contests like IEEEXtreme (Ranked #1 in Kenya) or IEEE Tech Ignite Hackathon (1st Runners Up at Strathmore), training deep vision models, or designing custom embedded hardware, I combine mathematical rigor with practical engineering to solve high-impact infrastructure challenges in Africa.
about.lookingFor: Currently scaling Proctor AI for the MEST AI Startup Program. Open to technical collaborations, AI research partnerships, and investment opportunities in educational infrastructure, automated assessment tools, and AI/hardware co-design.
about.beyond: International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) Participant representing Kenya at Alliance High School and IEEE Kenya Section Paper Writing Contest Runner-Up. Beyond engineering and training Olympiad teams, I explore classical music (Mozart's Requiem, piano, violin composition), pencil drawing, analytic number theory (Riemann hypothesis, prime gaps), and philosophy.
